spans.s: तैतल तैतल, अस्, m., N. of a man.
तैतलायनि, इस्, m. a patronymic from Taitala.

तैतिक्ष तैतिक्ष, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. तितिक्षा),
patient; (this word is also an adj. fr. तैतिक्ष्य.)

तैतिक्षव, अस्, m. a patronymic from Titi-
kṣu.
तैतिक्ष्य, अस्, m. a patronymic from Titikṣa.

तैतिर तैतिर, अस्, m. = तित्तिरि, a partridge;
(probably a wrong reading for तैत्तिर.)

तैत्तिर तैत्तिर, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. तित्तिरि), pro-
duced or coming from a partridge; sprung from the
sage Tittiri; (अस्), m. = तित्तिरि, a partridge; a rhino-
ceros; (अम्), n. a flock of partridges.
तैतिलि, इस्, m., N. of a man.

तैत्तिरि, इस्, m., N. of an ancient sage who was
an elder brother of Vaiśampāyana; N. of a son of
Kapota-roman and father of Punar-vasu.
तैत्तिरिक, अस्, m. one who catches partridges.

तैत्तिरीय, आस्, m. pl. the pupils of Tittiri, the
followers of the Taittirīya school of the Yajur-veda;
or the Yajur-veda itself, according to the version of
this school; see तैत्तिरीय-संहिता.
—तैत्तिरीय-
चरण, अस्, अम्, m. n. the school or sect of the
Taittirīyas.
—तैत्तिरीय-प्रातिशाख्य, अम्, n. the
Prātiśākhya of the Taittirīyas.
—तैत्तिरीय-ब्राह्-
मण, अम्, n. a Brāhmaṇa of the Taittirīya Yajur-
veda.
—तैत्तिरीय-शिक्षा, f. the pronunciation of
letters, accents, &c., according to the Taittirīyas.
—तैत्तिरीय-संहिता, f. the collection of the
hymns &c. of the dark or black Yajur-veda; (this,
the more ancient version of the Yajur-veda, was
called Taittirīya, as, handed, down by Tittiri, the
pupil of Yāska, the pupil of Vaiśampāyana; the more
modern or bright Yajur-veda being attributed to
Yājñavalkya, of the family of the Vājasaneyins: the
legend relates that the Yajus in its original form
was first taught by the sage Vaiśampāyana to twenty-
seven pupils, Yājñavalkya being deputed by him to
teach it to others; subsequently the sage being
offended with Yājñavalkya, bade him relinquish the
Veda committed to him, which he instantly disgorged
in a tangible form; whereupon the other disciples of
Vaiśampāyana receiving his command to pick it up,
assumed the form of partridges for that purpose, and
swallowed the texts, which were soiled, and hence
named ‘black,’ the other name तैत्तिरीय having
reference to the partridges. Yājñavalkya then had
recourse to the Sun, and from that deity received a
new revelation of the Yajus, which is sometimes
called ‘white,’ and sometimes from the patronymic
of Yājñavalkya, Vājasaneyin.)
—तैत्तिरीयारण्यक
(˚य-आर्˚), अम्, n. the Āraṇyaka of the Taittirīyas.
—तैत्तिरीयोपनिषद् (˚य-उप्˚), त्, f. the Upani-
shad of the Taittirīyas.

तैत्तिरीयक, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging to the Taitti-
rīya version of the Yajur-veda; (आस्), m. pl. = तैत्ति-
रीयास्, i. e. the followers of the Taittirīya school of
the Yajur-veda.
—तैत्तिरीयकोपनिषद् (˚क-उप्˚),
त्, f. the Upaniṣad of the Taittirīyas mentioned in
the Sarva-darśana-saṅgraha.
